concepts.label: Ambiguity governance locators

conditions: An evaluation was performed.

grounding.quote:
Recording. A result records its core value together with the predicate
evaluated and the original domain outcome, which is the refined value
where a refinement produced it. A mapping into the core never owns domain
meaning: the member, profile or adopting Product that defines the refined
value keeps it, and a consumer that needs the domain distinction reads the
domain outcome, never the core value alone (P1, P6).

constraints.statement: Every performed evaluation returns exactly one core value directly or through refinement. Constraint, judgment, frame, stop, work-step and effect results use this same core or a mapped refinement. Each result records its predicate and original domain outcome beside its core value. Domain meaning remains with its definer; consumers needing a domain distinction must read that outcome. No combination may hide failure, undecidability, non-performance or uncertain effects behind success.

grounding.quote:
Only
`satisfied` establishes the predicate. `falsified` establishes that the
predicate fails and names the counterexample. `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` establish neither, and each names what
would decide: the evidence, the missing relation or capability with its
owner where the subject gives one, or the basis repair. By support for the
predicate, `satisfied` stands above each other value, and the other four
are not ordered among themselves.

- an effect whose completion is unknown never maps to no effect or to
  completed.

constraints.statement: Only satisfied establishes its predicate; falsified establishes failure and names the counterexample. The other three establish neither and name deciding evidence, missing relation/capability and its owner where supplied, or basis repair. Satisfied is above the other four only in support for the predicate; those four have no mutual standing order. No refinement or mapping raises standing: failure or undecidability cannot become success, unknown effect completion cannot become no effect or completed. Failed, indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope and invalid-basis outcomes keep their declared-algebra outcomes rather than becoming satisfied. An unperformed required or planned evaluation has no closed result, maps to no core value, and cannot be reported as performed; missing results enter conjunction as the appropriate gap.

conditions: A refinement or further cause-based split is defined.

grounding.quote:
A further
refinement, by a member, profile, project or adopting Product, may split a
refined value by cause. The parent-value rule governs every such split:
each child value names its parent value and its cause and keeps its
parent's core value; a child that needs a different core value needs a
different parent value, which only the owner of the parent declares; and
no child takes `satisfied` from a parent that is not `satisfied`. No
further refinement raises a result's standing (P5, P6, P1). Purpose and
material relation: a consumer that reads a parent value reads the same
core value from each of its children, so a split by cause adds a domain
distinction and never changes what the parent establishes (P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Name the refinement's question and mapping predicate, map every value exactly once, add no core value, and keep indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis explicit. If cause would determine different core values, include cause in the refined value. Every child names parent and cause and preserves the parent's core value; changing that value requires a different parent declared only by the parent owner. Each defining member, profile or adopting Product states its mapping locally; ACTIVATION §3 is identified as owner of admission, activation and step refinements.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced domain mappings are not supplied.

conditions: Classifying an evaluation against the activated frame's declarations and the step's exercised capabilities.
exceptions: A claim can simultaneously have lawful out_of_frame and indeterminate grounds; the returned result names its chosen value and ground.
Failure to exercise a required declared capability does not prevent a result supported by a sufficient evaluation or applicable judgment without that capability.

grounding.quote:
Where the
  claim also depends on an undeclared relation or capability,
  `out_of_frame` and `indeterminate` each have a lawful ground; the result
  names the value it returns and that ground, and this boundary excludes
  neither (P5).

The evaluation's result and the step's stop state answer different
  questions, so the step's stop value never becomes the evaluation's
  result.

constraints.statement: Out_of_frame is grounded in a required undeclared material relation/capability, independently of exercise; it names the missing item, supplied owner and reconfiguration pressure. A result-material undefined term is such an undeclared relation because its meaning can alter the result without entering through a declared input. Indeterminate names the evidence needed to decide. An unexercised declared capability has no value of its own: sufficient evaluation or applicable judgment can still return a closed result with evidence, verdict and uncertainty, including falsification by A in A-and-B. Otherwise the evaluation is unperformed, construction availability carries incomplete, and work state carries the unexercised capability as residual. In either case unexercised B has no result and remains a planned-assessment gap; any known failure A survives. Step stop state never substitutes for evaluation result.

grounding.quote:
A step having produced a candidate never maps to the candidate's
fitness or acceptance, and acceptance is never inferred from a successful
step

constraints.statement: Candidate production establishes neither fitness nor acceptance. Availability, assessment and owner disposition remain distinct even when a disposition consumes the first two. A successful step, decision(holds), passing matrix, produced pack or work-result value does not by itself establish the separate assessment, acceptance or verdict. Acceptance boundaries and accepting authority belong to the referenced decision owner.
constraints.uncertainty: The owner-specific acceptance and disposition rules are external to the supplied sections.

grounding.quote:
Gaps. A conjunction with any item in the second or third input is never
`satisfied`. Its record names which kind of gap it has, not performed,
uncovered or both, and each item. An uncovered obligation is never
reported as satisfied or as an omitted planned assessment; a planned
assessment without a closed result is never reported as uncovered or as an
`indeterminate` component.

constraints.statement: Keep returned closed results with predicate/domain outcome separate from planned assessments without applicable closed results and from uncovered obligations R minus C. The second input includes unperformed, absent, stale, wrong-subject, wrong-basis or claim-incapable results; the third is required coverage addressed by no plan. Either gap prevents satisfied. Record each item and whether its kind is not performed, uncovered or both; never turn uncovered obligations into satisfied or omitted planned assessments, nor missing planned results into uncovered or indeterminate components.

conditions: Applicability of a held or newly performed result is assessed against the component basis required by the composite.
exceptions: A stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched evaluation may be reactivated on the current basis instead of returning invalid_basis.

grounding.quote:
- a component whose only held result is stale has no closed result
  applicable to the composite: on the basis the composite requires, its
  evaluation was not performed. It is a planned assessment without a
  closed result, in the second input, and a gap. Its stale value is
  neither counted as a returned result nor relabelled `invalid_basis` for
  the composite, and it stays in the record with its own basis;

constraints.statement: An evaluation performed on an unsupported stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched subject/basis returns invalid_basis for its own predicate, and that returned value is retained. A component held only on another or superseded basis has no applicable evaluation on the required basis: it is a gap, with its stale result recorded on the original basis, neither counted nor relabelled invalid_basis. Stale satisfied never supports the composite. Basis disagreement concerns only returned results individually bound to required component bases that fail a declared agreement or coherent-join relation. Do not answer one stale component both as a gap and invalid_basis; the composite has one reported value.

conditions: Results or conjunctions are joined.

grounding.quote:
Survival. Every known failure (a `falsified` result with its
counterexample), every planned assessment without a closed result and
every uncovered obligation is carried with the composite and survives every
join: combining conjunctions takes the union of known failures and of
planned assessments without a closed result, and recomputes uncovered
coverage over the combined obligations. A known failure and a gap of
either kind survive every join. Common agreement among contributors
cannot discard a constraint or a material counterexample that only one
contributor found. A missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate
mandatory result stays unresolved under the declared rule, and aggregate
satisfied status cannot replace it (P4b, P5).

constraints.statement: Carry every known falsification with counterexample, planned-assessment gap and uncovered obligation through every join. Union known failures and missing planned assessments and recompute uncovered coverage over combined obligations. Agreement cannot discard a constraint or a material counterexample found by one contributor. Missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate mandatory results remain unresolved and cannot be replaced by aggregate satisfied status. Every component keeps its predicate and domain outcome; uncertain effects, failures and undecided claims remain distinct, and satisfied for one predicate never counts for another.

grounding.quote:
Where
every mandatory result

constraints.statement: Satisfied is possible only with every mandatory result satisfied on valid applicable evidence, agreeing declared basis relations and no gaps; a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint also precludes success. If a mandatory result is non-satisfied, the declared rule chooses a non-satisfied value from returned values; there is no universal order. If every mandatory returned result is satisfied but declared basis relations disagree, report invalid_basis and retain gaps by kind. If every mandatory returned result is satisfied, bases agree and a gap remains, report indeterminate for the composite itself, retaining gap kinds without converting them to component results. Retain every nonmandatory falsified result with its predicate. With all mandatory results satisfied, agreeing bases and no gap, a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint falsifies the composite whoever found it; absent such a counterexample, use the declared rule over mandatory results.

grounding.quote:
The declared rule. A conjunction declares which results are mandatory; how
conflict and indeterminacy are handled; which basis relations must agree,
results on different bases combining only under a declared coherent
composite basis (§2, Basis); which decision authority owns the
conjunction; how results that are not mandatory count; and whether any
result may veto or defer the decision.
Conjunction does not transfer the semantic authority of a contributing
evaluation (P6, P4a).

constraints.statement: Declare mandatory results, handling of conflict and indeterminacy, required basis relations, owning decision authority, treatment of nonmandatory results, and any veto or deferral. Different bases combine only under a declared coherent composite basis. Conjunction transfers no contributor's semantic authority. A member or profile may declare only the choices the common rule leaves open.

conditions: Steps are composed under typed composition.

grounding.quote:
Composition of results. The result of composed steps for the outer
predicate is the conjunction of the steps' results, with the outer
contract's obligations as the required coverage. That each step returned
`satisfied` supports the outer predicate only where the refinement's
premises hold ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement),
Refinement).

composed steps exist only under typed composition; the composite carries both steps' step-produced facts, and its result for the outer predicate is the conjunction over the outer contract's obligations

constraints.statement: Typed step composition requires compatible preconditions, effects, results and authority, retains both steps' produced facts, and uses the outer contract's obligations as required coverage for conjunction. All steps being satisfied supports the outer predicate only under the applicable refinement premises. Combining frame results need not compose frames or establish a categorical join; required composition laws must be stated.
constraints.uncertainty: ACTIVATION refinement and RF-010 conditions are referenced but not supplied.

conditions: The relevant result-family situation applies.

grounding.quote: for an evaluation that depends on a concept imported from another member, a missing source meaning, adoption or authority binding is a relation the frame does not declare, and a changed member or basis whose applicability is not re-established cannot support the evaluation
a categorical claim is established only with its demonstration, and without it is a hypothesis

constraints.statement: For imported concepts, missing source meaning, adoption or authority binding grounds out_of_frame; changed member/basis applicability not re-established cannot support evaluation. Every transformation records preserved, introduced and removed material, external witnesses and residuals; no fact is lost unrecorded. A reference substitutes for a body only when it supports the same consuming decision; shortfall is a residual, never success, and carrier/budget limits cannot trim required members. Values differ lawfully only through a declared relation, not preference, probabilistic choice or human presence. Similar computation can propose shared machinery but establishes no identity or authority; each instance retains responsibility and binding. Categorical claims require demonstrations or remain hypotheses. These are subject-stated laws, not executed transformations or established proofs here.
constraints.uncertainty: The detailed transformation fields, categorical demonstration requirements, import declarations and accepted-design conditions reside in referenced sections outside the supplied text.

conditions: A cited consumer applies a Results family rule.

grounding.quote:
Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).
where a refusal keeps its predicate and `refusal(basis)` is a closed result, not a gap

constraints.statement: The named consumer loci apply owned rules without adding decisions. RF-012, AC-007 and review results apply the core and add only mapped refinements. Consumers preserve local vocabulary, residuals, re-entry law, classifications and predicates beside core values, including not-applicable versus meeting-an-axiom distinctions. Unrun cases on the current revision, clean skips, unresolved release dispositions, unevaluated applicable axioms and unrun verification have no result. Unselected claims and uncovered ledger rows are uncovered coverage, not falsified components. refusal(basis) is a closed result, not a gap; partial_effect residuals survive joins. A failed run falsifies only that run's predicate. A stale held result is a gap, whereas a performed stale-tuple audit can return invalid_basis for its own predicate. Work completion requires every applicable obligation; the cited usability claim requires all four results and explicit conjunction. A contraction records total projection-to-accepted-atom mapping; intentional omission/flattening declares accepted loss and a failure condition. Applicable equivalence/functor/structure-preservation claims require their demonstrations.
constraints.uncertainty: Consumer-specific definitions, the identity of the four usability results, and demonstration criteria are external; their asserted application roles are retained without reconstructing those bodies.

conditions: A family rule's stated instance premises apply.

grounding.quote:
Its instance premises are: (a) a construction
with the governing basis bound at intake under ACTIVATION §1 and the
material assumptions, together written Γ here; (b) a declared domain Ω of cases, each with the inputs,
behaviour and environment material to an obligation; (c) a checker with
declared observations and an admitted evaluation relation. They are
conditions of the situations the family governs, not commitments.

constraints.statement: The six assurance subsections share one owner and their consumers introduce no second relation or additional decision. Instance premises are situational conditions, not commitments. Step-law owners choose approximate adequacy/bounds; construction-design owners choose concurrency/branch/external-effect composition laws; obligation owner and assessor activation choose Ω and interpretation; assessment-frame owner chooses T and π; strategy owner chooses compared paths; admitted work authority under the Product chooses risk policy/threshold; realisation chooses dependency representation/selection model; RELEASE §8 and Product own mandatory gates; tenant a_c design under AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS chooses carrier/checker/projections. Writing a proof obligation does not discharge it. A failing scenario supports actual-behaviour disagreement only with supported observation binding; unsupported numerical confidence remains unresolved. The interpretation recording support kinds is described as a derived view, not a consumer of the formal-representation rule.
constraints.uncertainty: Commitment definitions and referenced owner bodies are not supplied; their table attributions are source claims.

conditions: A preservation step is claimed.

grounding.quote: For all x, x':  P_i(x) and F_i(x, x')  implies  P_(i+1)(x').

constraints.statement: State boundary domains, transition relation and property, with the universally quantified obligation: for all x,x', P_i(x) and F_i(x,x') imply P_(i+1)(x'). Account for outcomes, effects and assumptions material to the claim. A successful-completion-only relation establishes nothing about refusal, failure, interruption or unknown effects; those retain their result, authority and recovery contracts. Actual execution's conformance to F_i is a separate obligation.
constraints.uncertainty: No particular transition is supplied or proved; referenced recovery and authority contracts remain external.

conditions: An end-to-end construction claim is made.

grounding.quote:
An end-to-end argument establishes the initial condition, each step's
applicable premises, compatibility at each composition boundary, and the
connection from the final property to Z. The preceding postcondition
must establish the next precondition, or the missing condition must be
acquired and justified. Concurrency, alternative branches and external effects
require their applicable composition law; a sequential drawing does not
establish one. Local success alone establishes neither composition
compatibility nor Z. Preservation is distinct from progress, termination
and the availability of a suitable next step (P4a, P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Establish the initial condition, each applicable step premise, every boundary's compatibility and final-property connection to Z. A preceding postcondition must establish the next precondition, or the missing condition must be acquired and justified. Concurrency, alternatives and external effects require their applicable composition laws; sequential drawings and local successes establish neither those laws nor Z. Preservation does not establish progress, termination or availability of a suitable next step.

grounding.quote:
Exact transformations preserve the declared meaning. Approximate
transformations state their adequacy relation and an established bound
for the complete composition; local tolerances cannot be assumed to add or
to remain unchanged. [ACTIVATION §4 Refinement](ACTIVATION.md#refinement),
Exact and approximate steps, owns the per-step law and applies this
obligation to refinement steps. A
change to the governing outcome or meaning follows its owner and the
successor rules of SPEC_METHOD §4 and RELEASE §9 (P1, P6).

constraints.statement: Exact transformations preserve declared meaning. Approximate ones state adequacy relation and an established complete-composition bound; local tolerances cannot be assumed additive or unchanged. Governing outcome/meaning changes follow their owner and successor rules. The algorithmic account states required operation, informational account retained meaning/distinctions, and computational binding realised work/observations. Claims across accounts identify maps and preservation obligations; human, machine or mixed execution alone discharges none. Commuting-diagram, functor and equivalence claims require categorical demonstration.
constraints.uncertainty: Per-step refinement, successor rules and the complete categorical demonstration specification are external.

conditions: An assertion interprets or claims to establish a source obligation under Γ and Ω.

grounding.quote:
Q_r implies q_t                   : q_t is a necessary condition of Q_r.
q_t implies Q_r                   : establishing q_t is sufficient for Q_r.
(q_1 and ... and q_n) implies Q_r : the stated conjunction is sufficient.
```

These implications are conditional on Γ and Ω. Passing a check of a
necessary condition does not establish the full obligation. A conjunction
requires its own coverage and compatibility argument; a collection of
passing tests does not supply it by its count (P1, P6, P5).

constraints.statement: Retain source scope, conditions, exceptions and permitted alternatives; identifier/digest authentication does not prove interpretive fidelity. Declare the assertion's breadth and implication direction: Q_r ⇒ q_t is necessary, q_t ⇒ Q_r sufficient, and conjunction(q_1…q_n) ⇒ Q_r collectively sufficient, all conditional on Γ and Ω. Passing a necessary condition establishes no full obligation. Sufficient conjunction claims require their own coverage and compatibility arguments, not a count of passing tests.

conditions: A checker soundness or source-satisfaction claim is made.
exceptions: A relation admitting sound satisfied and indeterminate conclusions need not always decide.
A restricted deterministic model retains its restricted scope.

grounding.quote:
For every s in Ω:
  (π(s), sat) in T  implies  q_t(s).
  (π(s), fal) in T  implies  not q_t(s).

constraints.statement: Universal soundness covers every admitted conclusion for every s in Ω: (π(s),sat) ∈ T implies q_t(s), and (π(s),fal) ∈ T implies not q_t(s). Identify support and unresolved parts of each claimed direction; the actual checker needs its own conformance account. Until oracle fidelity is established, observed passes and failures remain observations, not established satisfaction or falsification of the source obligation. Support actual acquisition of the facts represented by π; an ideal observation map proves no instrument/actor/execution fidelity. T alone supplies no probabilities; probabilistic claims require a declared distribution. Indeterminate remains distinct from non-performance and unresolved work/coverage states.

conditions: A checker claims always to decide q_t correctly using π alone.

grounding.quote:
If two admissible cases have the same observation but opposite truth
values, that observation cannot support a sound complete decision between
them; further evidence, a justified narrower scope or an indeterminate
judgment is required. In a classical set model this condition permits a
predicate on the image of π; it establishes neither an executable decision
procedure nor its cost. Unknown effects and unavailable observations
retain their distinctions from falsehood and from an evaluation that was
not performed (Results) (P3, P1, P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Require ∀s,s'∈Ω: π(s)=π(s') ⇒ q_t(s)=q_t(s'). Indistinguishable admissible cases with opposite truth values require further evidence, justified scope narrowing or indeterminate; they cannot support sound complete decision from those observations. In a classical set model, the condition permits a predicate on image(π), but proves neither executable decision procedure nor cost. Unknown effects and unavailable observations are not falsehood or non-performance.

conditions: Assurance claims use derivations, executions or comparisons.

grounding.quote:
Assurance accounts for
shared specifications, interpretations, tools, fixtures, observations,
copied material and other material failure causes. Different actors,
model families or codebases do not establish statistical independence.
Porting retains authorship and common dependencies (EVALUATION §3 and the
Cross-Synthesis rule of the Product that owns this corpus). Repeating
evidence does not create a new independent observation.

constraints.statement: Both assertion and execution provenance are needed for their respective claims; execution records cannot justify the expected answer, and authentication establishes neither provenance. Implementation-derived tests may support regression/local properties, but repeating implementation decisions supplies no independent upstream-fidelity justification. A shorter assertion path's inspectability/executability requires support and guarantees no correctness, coverage or independence. Distinct valid implementations may differ within an acceptable relation, so equality need not be the oracle. Agreement permits correctness or shared error; disagreement requires diagnosis and identifies no faulty party alone. Account for all material shared causes, preserve ported authorship/dependencies, and do not infer independence from different actors, model families, codebases or repeated evidence. Agreement with an incorrect common model cannot validate it against reality; governing expectations require purpose and externally owned observations, while corrections preserve counterexamples and follow change authority.
constraints.uncertainty: Cross-Synthesis, diagnosis and change-authority details are referenced but not supplied.

conditions: A numerical assurance claim is made.

grounding.quote:
P(V | E, Γ) =
  P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ)
  / [P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ) + P(E | not V, Γ) P(not V | Γ)].
```

The denominator must be nonzero. E can include agreement, disagreement or other
observations; its likelihood under both faulty and non-faulty conditions
matters. The formula supplies no missing likelihood or prior, and a
numerical posterior is no stronger than its model and evidence.

constraints.statement: State population/uncertainty, priors, likelihoods, shared causes and calibration limits. The stated Bayesian posterior is P(E|V,Γ)P(V|Γ) divided by P(E|V,Γ)P(V|Γ)+P(E|not V,Γ)P(not V|Γ), requiring nonzero denominator. E may be agreement, disagreement or other observations; both faulty and nonfaulty likelihoods matter. The equation supplies no missing prior/likelihood and adds no strength beyond model/evidence. Calibration by samples or injected defects supports only its justified relation to operational failures. Unsupported numeric confidence stays unresolved.
constraints.uncertainty: No numerical inputs, model calibration or posterior are supplied.

conditions: Joint miss or detection probability is claimed.
exceptions: Zero-probability prefixes must be handled without inventing undefined conditional probabilities.

grounding.quote:
Conditional terms require defined conditioning events; zero-probability
prefixes are handled without inventing a conditional value. Replacing
those terms with `P(M_i | V, Γ)` requires conditional independence under
the declared model. One minus the joint miss probability is the chance of
at least one detection under those same conditions; it is not the
probability that the whole product is correct. Agreement does not
necessarily increase confidence when shared causes or new information
change the model (P6, P1).

constraints.statement: Use the exact conditional factorization P(M_1 and … and M_n|V,Γ)=product_i P(M_i|V,Γ,M_1,…,M_(i−1)) with defined conditioning events. Replacing the factors by P(M_i|V,Γ) requires conditional independence in the declared model. One minus joint miss probability means at least one detection under the same conditions, not whole-product correctness. Agreement need not increase confidence when shared causes or new information change the model.

conditions: An assurance strategy is selected.

grounding.quote:
Risk model. The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects the required
assurance for the stated risk, obligations and resource limits. That
selection identifies material failure consequences, coverage and
uncertainty, and the conditions for action or acceptance. Additional
evidence can strengthen a claim only within its applicability and
dependence account; neither a test count nor an assumed preference for more checks
substitutes for that account (P6, P5).

constraints.statement: The actor exercising admitted work authority selects required assurance for stated risk, obligations and resources, identifying failure consequences, coverage, uncertainty and action/acceptance conditions. More evidence strengthens claims only within applicability/dependence accounting, never by test count or preference alone. Qualitative evidence and stated limits remain usable under governing policy; there is no universal probability threshold or requirement to estimate every test. A cheaper plan cannot waive safety, authority or acceptance conditions.

conditions: Selecting checks or excluding them after change Δ.

grounding.quote:
The representation of these dependencies is the tenant's choice; no
exhaustive graph database is required. Excluding a check requires
supported coverage of its material dependencies and a reason the change
cannot invalidate the intended reused claim; an absent edge is not
evidence of non-influence. Unknown impact widens reassessment or leaves
the dependent assurance unresolved. New obligations or cases create
assessment work even when no existing check covers them. A mandatory
gate, an assessment that the governing policy requires irrespective of
selection ([RELEASE §8](RELEASE.md#8-acceptance)), remains applicable
(P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Cover changed facts, affected dependents and material transitive assertion/execution/evidence-use dependencies conservatively. Exclusion requires supported dependency coverage and a reason the change cannot invalidate the reused claim; absent edges prove no non-influence. Unknown impact widens reassessment or leaves dependent assurance unresolved. New obligations/cases require assessment even without existing checks. Reassessment includes S_Δ, new obligations and all applicable mandatory gates. Selection produces no execution evidence, and failed/indeterminate results retain standing.

conditions: Existing evidence is proposed for a new subject and basis.

grounding.quote:
Retention establishes the material validity conditions on the new
subject: the claim and its scope still apply, its assertion and
observation basis remain justified, and the affected dependencies are
unchanged or covered by an established preservation relation. The
original evidence keeps its original subject; a new applicability
relation permits its use. A changed hash alone establishes neither
invalidity nor equivalence. A corrected run is not an unchanged independent
test of the correction: the corrected subject carries its own evidence.
Known failures, unresolved coverage and their
citations remain visible until a supported repair, a reassessment or an
authorised change of obligation disposes of them (P3, P4b, P6).

constraints.statement: E_new = retain_applicable(E_old,new_subject,new_basis) union E_reassessed. Retention establishes continuing claim/scope applicability, justified assertion and observation bases, and unchanged dependencies or established preservation. Original evidence retains original subject; a new applicability relation permits reuse. Hash change alone establishes neither invalidity nor equivalence. A corrected run supplies evidence for its corrected subject, not an unchanged independent test of its correction. Known failures, unresolved coverage and citations remain visible until supported repair, reassessment or authorized obligation change disposes of them.

conditions: Requirements, refinements, realisation or assurance selection change, or recovery occurs.

grounding.quote:
If a governing requirement changes, dependent expectations may need
authorised revision as well as new execution. A correction in a
refinement revisits the affected obligations and their links to both the
requirement and the realisation. A correction in the realisation
reassesses the affected implementation and integration under the
still-applicable obligations. These are semantic dependency boundaries,
not file or directory boundaries. Recovery reacquires current reality and
invalidates affected claims; it need not erase valid work or rerun every
check ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)) (P3, P6).

its three
invalidators are kinds of change Δ, and a closed result is affected when
its `D*(t)` meets `I(Δ)` (P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Requirement changes may need authorized expectation revision and new execution; refinement corrections revisit affected obligations and links to requirement/realisation; realisation corrections reassess affected implementation/integration under still-applicable obligations. These are semantic, not directory boundaries. Recovery reacquires reality and invalidates affected claims without requiring erasure of valid work or rerunning all checks. Assurance completeness can combine applicable retained and new evidence and differs from universal execution freshness. Optimize impact-analysis, acquisition, execution and assessment costs together, distinguishing predictions from measurements, within required assurance/risk/gates. Cheap uncovered selections are insufficient. Broad/uncertain impact, changed selection model, release rules or missed dependencies can justify wider testing; full suites remain available, may have gaps and have no universal cadence. Failures require diagnosis and authorized response; the next action may gather evidence before repair is justified. Closed-result/handoff invalidation applies the D*(t)–I(Δ) intersection rule.
constraints.uncertainty: The three ACTIVATION §7 invalidators and governing gate policies are not supplied.

conditions: Representing or demonstrating the candidate's assurance obligations.
exceptions: An unproved universal claim may remain unresolved while bounded construction and assurance proceed where governing conditions permit.

grounding.quote:
Mathematical proof, exhaustive checks of a finite model, sampled tests and
observed use retain their distinct scopes. Finite examples do not prove
the universal implications above. An unproved universal claim can remain
unresolved while bounded construction and assurance proceed where their
governing conditions permit them (P5, P6).

The existing member and integrated criteria assess these owners and their
consumers ([EVALUATION §6](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations)).
Source semantics, formal fidelity and actual use retain their separate
evidence; these obligations create no seventh criterion and do not make
each test a theorem-proving exercise (P6).

constraints.statement: Represent material obligations/dependencies under the Product's constraint-surface fidelity rule through AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS and acquired views, preserving all five support kinds.
